outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Foundations of LLM-Enhanced Tabular Learning
outline.description: This chapter introduces the reader to the intersection of Large Language Models (LLMs) and tabular data analysis. It covers the shift from end-to-end LLM prediction to leveraging LLMs as domain experts for feature engineering, highlighting the specific challenges of few-shot learning in tabular domains.
subtopics: The Potential of Generalist Models for Tabular Data
Limitations of End-to-End LLM Inference for High-Dimensional Data
The Role of Prior Knowledge in Addressing Data Scarcity
Definition of Feature Engineering via Natural Language Reasoning

outline.description: This chapter details the structural design of the FeatLLM framework. It explains how the problem is decomposed into logical steps and outlines the mechanism of converting AI-generated natural language into executable machine learning features.
subtopics: Overview of the Feature-First Inference Paradigm
Two-Step Reasoning Process: Causal Inference and Rule Derivation
Structuring Inputs: Prompt Components (Task, Features, Examples)
Guiding LLM Output: Instruction Templates for Rule Generation

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Prompt Engineering and Rule Extraction Strategies
outline.description: A deep dive into the specific techniques used to instruct the LLM. This chapter breaks down how prompts are constructed to force high-quality reasoning and how validation logic is used to safely extract backend code.
subtopics: Filtering Spurious Correlations via Separated Reasoning Steps
